# Orbit Outdoor policies
## Returns
You can return any unused item within 30 days of delivery for a full refund. Items must be unused and in their original packaging.
## Return shipping
Return shipping is free on orders over $75. Under $75, a $6.95 return label is taken off the refund.
## Refunds
Refunds go back to the original payment method within 5 business days of the return arriving. Refunds over $200 must be approved by a member of the support team.
## Exchanges
Exchanging for a different size is free if the new size is in stock.
## Shipping
Standard shipping takes 3 to 5 business days. Express takes 1 to 2 business days.
## Damaged items
Send a photo within 7 days of delivery and we send a replacement or a full refund.

steps.title: Create memory.py
steps.body: This class is Scout's short-term memory. It trims the chat to the last few customer turns, and pins key facts like the order number so they never fall out.
actions: Create a new file **memory.py** in the **scout** folder and paste the code below.
Save it, then run `python memory.py`. This tries the class on its own, without calling the model.

values.label: memory.py
values.value:
"""Scout's memory: the recent turns of the chat, plus facts that never fall out."""
import re

ORDER_ID = re.compile(r"\bORB-\d{5}\b", re.IGNORECASE)
NAME = re.compile(r"\bmy name is ([A-Za-z]+)", re.IGNORECASE)


def block_type(block):
    """Blocks from the SDK are objects; blocks you write yourself are dicts."""
    return block.get("type") if isinstance(block, dict) else getattr(block, "type", None)


class Conversation:
    def __init__(self, max_turns=10):
        self.max_turns = max_turns  # customer turns sent with each call
        self.messages = []          # short-term memory: what the model sees
        self.facts = {}             # pinned facts: they survive trimming

    def add_user(self, text):
        """A message the customer typed. Key details are pinned as facts."""
        order = ORDER_ID.search(text)
        if order:
            self.facts["order_id"] = order.group(0).upper()
        name = NAME.search(text)
        if name:
            self.facts["name"] = name.group(1).capitalize()
        self.drop_old_thinking()
        self.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": text})
        self.trim()

    def add_assistant(self, content):
        """Scout's turn: the response's content blocks, or plain text."""
        self.messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": content})

    def add_tool_results(self, results):
        """All tool results from one step, in one user message."""
        self.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": results})

    def drop_old_thinking(self):
        """The model's thinking blocks are tied to the exact conversation it saw.
        Trimming turns or pinning a new fact changes that conversation, so when a
        new turn starts, earlier turns keep only their text and tool calls."""
        for m in self.messages:
            if m["role"] == "assistant" and isinstance(m["content"], list):
                kept = [b for b in m["content"] if block_type(b) not in ("thinking", "redacted_thinking")]
                m["content"] = kept or [{"type": "text", "text": "(no reply)"}]

    def trim(self):
        """Keep the last max_turns customer turns. Cut only where a turn
        starts, so a tool call is never separated from its result."""
        starts = [i for i, m in enumerate(self.messages)
                  if m["role"] == "user" and isinstance(m["content"], str)]
        if len(starts) > self.max_turns:
            self.messages = self.messages[starts[-self.max_turns]:]

    def system_prompt(self, base):
        """The base prompt plus the pinned facts, rebuilt for every call."""
        if not self.facts:
            return base
        lines = "\n".join(f"- {key}: {value}" for key, value in self.facts.items())
        return f"{base}\n\nFacts about this customer (always use them):\n{lines}"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    convo = Conversation(max_turns=2)
    convo.add_user("Hi, my name is Ravi and my order is orb-10533.")
    convo.add_assistant("Thanks, Ravi! How can I help?")
    convo.add_user("Can I return the foam mat?")
    convo.add_assistant("Yes, within 30 days of delivery.")
    convo.add_user("And the sleeping bag?")
    print(len(convo.messages), "messages kept. Oldest:", convo.messages[0]["content"])
    print(convo.system_prompt("You are Scout."))

steps.tip: Trimming cuts only where a customer turn starts. If you cut by message count instead, you could keep a tool result and drop the tool call it answers, and the API would reject the request. Scout also drops its old thinking blocks when a new turn starts: the API ties each one to the exact conversation it saw, and trimming or a new fact changes that conversation.

values.value:
"""Scout with memory, policy search, a plan-first prompt and a step limit."""
import anthropic

from memory import Conversation
from tools import TOOLS, run_tool

client = anthropic.Anthropic()  # reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
MODEL = "claude-opus-5-5"
MAX_STEPS = 6   # tool rounds allowed for each customer message
MAX_TURNS = 4   # small on purpose, so you can watch trimming; use 10 or more for real

SYSTEM = """You are Scout, Orbit Outdoor's support assistant. Orbit sells hiking, camping and climbing gear online.

How you work:
- If a request has more than one part, first write a short numbered plan (one to three steps), then use your tools.
- For any question about returns, refunds, shipping, exchanges or damaged items, call search_policy and answer only from the sections it returns.
- If those sections don't cover the question, say so and offer to pass it to the support team. Never guess, and never promise anything the policy doesn't say.
- Use calculate for any arithmetic.
- You can't look up orders yet. If a customer needs order details, say a teammate will check them.
- Never ask for card numbers or passwords.
- Keep replies short, warm and clear."""

convo = Conversation(max_turns=MAX_TURNS)


def answer(question):
    convo.add_user(question)
    for step in range(MAX_STEPS):  # always a step limit
        response = client.messages.create(model=MODEL, max_tokens=16000,
                                          system=convo.system_prompt(SYSTEM),
                                          tools=TOOLS, messages=convo.messages)
        convo.add_assistant(response.content)
        if response.stop_reason != "tool_use":
            return next(b.text for b in response.content if b.type == "text")
        results = []
        for block in response.content:
            if block.type == "text":
                print(f"  [plan] {block.text}")
            elif block.type == "tool_use":
                print(f"  [tool] {block.name} {block.input}")
                try:
                    output = run_tool(block.name, block.input)
                    results.append({"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": block.id, "content": output})
                except Exception as err:
                    results.append({"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": block.id,
                                    "content": f"Error: {err}", "is_error": True})
        convo.add_tool_results(results)  # all results in one message
    reply = "This is taking me more steps than it should, so I'm passing it to a person on our team."
    convo.add_assistant(reply)
    return reply


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("Scout is ready. Type quit to stop.")
    while True:
        question = input("\nYou: ").strip()
        if question.lower() == "quit":
            break
        if question:
            print(f"\nScout: {answer(question)}")
            oldest = convo.messages[0]["content"][:40]
            print(f"  (memory: {len(convo.messages)} messages, oldest: {oldest!r}, facts: {convo.facts})")

steps.check: You see **Scout is ready. Type quit to stop.**, and typing `quit` ends the program without an error.

blocks.title: What should Scout remember?
blocks.intro: Three situations from Scout's first weeks with memory, retrieval and planning. Each looks small, and each could cost Orbit a customer's trust.

scenarios.title: A card number in the chat
scenarios.situation: Tom wants to know whether his payment went through, and pastes his full card number and expiry date into the chat. Priya's new long-term memory saves facts from each chat into a customer profile, so Scout can greet people next time. This morning's memory log shows what it saved for Tom.

context.label: Memory log
lines: Tom: did my payment go through? my card is 4111 1111 1111 1111, exp 08/28

question.stem: What should Scout's memory do with that card number?

options.text: Keep it only in short-term memory, since the chat is trimmed after ten turns anyway
options.rationale: Trimming only changes what the model sees later. The number still sits in the history for ten turns, and it has already been sent to the model and written to the logs.

options.text: Save it encrypted in Tom's profile, so he can skip typing it next time
options.rationale: Encryption lowers the risk but doesn't remove it, and no job Scout does needs a card number. Data you never store can't leak.

options.text: Mask it before anything is saved or logged, never store it, and tell Tom kindly that Scout never needs card details
options.rationale: Scout checks payments by order number and email, so the card adds risk and no value. Masking it before saving keeps it out of profiles, logs and future prompts.

hints: Which of Scout's jobs actually needs a card number?
Think about everywhere a message goes: the prompt, the history, the logs and the profile.

scenarios.debrief: Store the least personal data that does the job. Redact patterns like card numbers before a message is saved, logged or sent on, and keep long-term memory to useful, low-risk facts such as preferences. When a customer overshares, Scout can say kindly that it never needs card details.

scenarios.title: The 60-day answer
scenarios.situation: Leo asked Priya to let search_policy look through every file in docs, so Scout can use the size guides too. Today a customer whose boots arrived 45 days ago asked about a return, and Scout said yes. Orbit's policy is 30 days. Last year's returns file is still in the folder.

context.label: Scout's trace
lines: < You can return any unused item within 60 days of delivery...
< You can return any unused item within 30 days of delivery...
Scout: Good news! You have 60 days, so you're still in time.

options.text: Remove last year's file from docs, and add a last-updated date to every policy file
options.rationale: The search did its job: it found what was in the folder. Retrieval can only be as current as its sources, and dates make stale text easy to spot and filter out.

options.text: Tell Scout in the system prompt to always pick the smaller number of days
options.rationale: That patches one number. The next outdated file will disagree about something else, and the stale text is still there to be retrieved.

options.text: Return the top 5 chunks instead of the top 2
options.rationale: The correct chunk was already retrieved. More chunks means more conflicting text in the prompt, not less.

hints: Did the search fail, or did it faithfully find what was in the folder?
Fix the source, not the symptom.

scenarios.debrief: Treat your documents as part of the agent. Keep one current version of each policy, move old ones out of the searched folder, and date every file so retrieval can prefer the newest. Then add a test case: a return 45 days after delivery should get a no.

scenarios.title: The exchange that never ends
scenarios.situation: Ana asks to swap her tent for the 3-person one. A test copy of Scout, started without a step limit, keeps re-planning: it checks stock, tries another colour, then checks the first one again. Sam spots it in the logs twenty minutes later.

context.label: Scout's trace
lines: step 3   think: maybe another colour is in stock
step 5   think: try another colour again

options.text: Tell Scout in the prompt to keep trying until the tent is back in stock
options.rationale: That makes the loop longer, not shorter. Sam's stock sheet won't change while Scout keeps checking it.

options.text: Add a step limit in code; when it's reached, stop and hand off with a summary of what was tried
options.rationale: The limit doesn't rely on the model choosing to stop. Ana gets an honest answer, and a person starts from the summary instead of from scratch.

options.text: Remove check_stock so Scout can't get stuck on it
options.rationale: Then Scout can't answer stock questions at all. The tool isn't the problem; the missing exit is.

hints: Which kind of limit still works when the model keeps asking for tools?

scenarios.debrief: Every agent loop needs an exit that lives in code: a step limit, and ideally a check for the same call repeated with the same input. When the limit is reached, Scout stops, writes down what it tried, and hands off. An identical call made twice in a row is a strong sign the agent is stuck.

items.stem: Grace's chat with Scout is ending. Along the way she said Ridge boots fit her best in size 39. Priya's new long-term memory saves a few details for each customer. What should it save for Grace?

options.text: That Ridge boots fit her best in size 39, so her next visit can start from there
Her home address and birthday, in case a future chat with Scout ever needs them
Her whole chat, word for word, so Scout can reread everything on her next visit
That size 39 had 2 pairs in stock today, so Scout can skip the stock check next time

items.stem: Elena's chat with Scout has reached 45 turns, and each reply now takes noticeably longer. Priya says Claude Opus 5.5 has a 1 million token window, so nothing needs to change. What is the best response?

options.text: Move the chat to a model with an even larger window, so it never gets close to the limit
Start a fresh chat every ten turns, so each request stays small and every reply is fast
Agree: the chat is far below the window, so speed and cost stay the same as turn one
Keep recent turns word for word, condense older ones into a short note, and pin key facts

items.stem: Orbit adds a 40-page care guide to docs. Priya splits it every 50 words to keep chunks small, and now Scout's washing advice for the storm jacket stops halfway through the steps. What is the best fix?

options.text: Switch from keyword scoring to embeddings, so the right chunk gets a higher score
Paste the whole care guide into the system prompt, so no instruction is ever cut off
Split at the guide's headings, so each chunk is a passage that makes sense on its own
Return the top 10 chunks instead of 2, so the missing halves come back along with them

items.stem: Owen wants to return his $310 jacket. Scout's plan: 1. get_order to check delivery. 2. search_policy for returns. 3. Refund $310 to his card. 4. Tell Owen the money is on its way. What should change?

options.text: Drop step 2, since the return rules are simple enough for Scout to answer from memory
Steps 3 and 4: a refund over $200 needs a person to approve it, so Scout can't promise it
Cut it to two steps, since a four-step plan is too much for a single return question
Swap steps 1 and 2, so Scout reads the return policy before it looks up Owen's order

items.stem: To save money, Priya tries a fixed script: always get_order, then track_parcel, then reply. On Ravi's order, still processing with no tracking number, it breaks. Why does Scout's ReAct loop cope?

options.text: It reads each result before choosing its next step, so it skips tracking with no number
It writes its whole plan before any tool call, so the calls always come in the right order
It keeps retrying track_parcel until ParcelPath has a tracking number for the order
Its step limit stops the failed tracking call before the error can ever reach Ravi

items.stem: A family-run guesthouse's assistant answers from its house guide. A guest asks the check-in time, whether parking is free, and if she can bring her dog. Search returns check-in and parking, nothing on pets. What should it do?

options.text: Answer all three, saying small dogs are usually welcome, as they are at most guesthouses
Answer check-in and parking from the guide, and leave the dog out so nothing is guessed
Pass the whole request to the owner, since one of its three parts isn't in the guide
Answer check-in and parking from the guide, say pets aren't covered, and offer the owner
